summary: Review index insurance terms, basis risk, subsidies, partners and claims workflows. Explore this practical course for programme and insurance managers.
lede: Agricultural index insurance operations training helps agricultural insurers, programme managers and risk-financing teams review product terms and delivery workflows. Participants practise checking policy schedules and basis-risk disclosures, reconciling subsidy records, and mapping partner and claims controls. It uses ISO 31000 and the IAIS Insurance Core Principles as operational references, not as substitutes for actuarial pricing or applicable insurance requirements.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for the institutional controls and client-facing operations of agricultural index insurance. This course is designed for: Agricultural insurance product managers reviewing index policy terms and client value. Agricultural insurance operations managers overseeing enrolment, premium records and claims workflows. Government agriculture risk-financing officers managing premium subsidy administration and programme reporting. Agricultural insurance claims officers documenting trigger decisions, payouts and client queries. Insurance distribution partnership managers monitoring cooperative and intermediary performance. Cooperative insurance coordinators supporting farmer enrolment and policy communication. Agricultural extension programme managers explaining policy triggers and basis risk to clients. Inclusive insurance specialists reviewing customer treatment and policy disclosures. Agricultural reinsurance liaison officers coordinating product and claims information across counterparties. Development-partner programme officers monitoring agricultural insurance delivery and subsidy controls.
modules: Index Insurance Mandate and Client Value
prerequisites: Working familiarity with agricultural insurance, agricultural programme delivery or insurance operations is recommended. No actuarial qualification or programming skills are required.
